topics.name: Modal + have + past participle (must have, should have, can't have)

options: Mathilde had no rich dresses and a jewels.
Mathilde had no rich dresses and many jewel.
Mathilde had no rich dresses and no jewels.
questions.rule: No + plural noun is fine (no jewels); a needs a singular noun and many needs a plural one.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct past forms.
options: She teared open the envelope and drew out a card.
She tore open the envelope and drew out a card.
She tore open the envelope and drawed out a card.
questions.rule: Tear and draw are irregular: their past forms are tore and drew.

options: You must have made a mistake, madam.
You must had made a mistake, madam.
You must have make a mistake, madam.
questions.rule: To guess about the past, use must have + past participle: must have made.

options: Each guests received an invitation card.
Each guest received an invitation card.
Each guest received a invitation card.
questions.rule: Each takes a singular noun (guest), and an goes before a vowel sound (an invitation).

options: Loisel asked her whether had she taken the cab's number.
Loisel asked her that whether she had taken the cab's number.
Loisel asked her whether she had taken the cab's number.
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order (she had taken) and no that before whether.

options: If they had found the necklace, they would not borrowed money.
If they would have found the necklace, they would not have borrowed money.
If they had found the necklace, they would not have borrowed money.
questions.rule: Third conditional: If + had + past participle, then would have + past participle.

options: Many money was needed to replace the necklace.
Much money was needed to replace the necklace.
Much money were needed to replace the necklace.
questions.rule: Money is uncountable: use much and a singular verb was.

options: Madame Forestier need not to have worried about her necklace.
Madame Forestier need not have worry about her necklace.
Madame Forestier need not have worried about her necklace.
questions.rule: Need not have + past participle (no 'to') means something was done but was not necessary.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Simple present with a third person singular subject takes the -s form: washes.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Before a noun, use the possessive determiner her: her friend.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Should have + past participle talks about the past: should have returned.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a past reporting verb (wrote), has broken moves back to had broken; the day before also needs the past perfect.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Third conditional: the if-part takes the past perfect - If Mathilde had not lost.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both verbs share was (passive), so both need the past participle: bought and paid.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Can't have + past participle says something was impossible in the past: can't have known.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Neither ... nor with two singular nouns takes a singular verb: was.

questions.after: rich friend from her school days.
questions.rule: Rich starts with a consonant sound, so use a; much is only for uncountable nouns.

questions.after: the necklace around her neck and looked in the mirror.
questions.rule: Both actions are in the past (looked), so use fastened.
After a modal like must, always use the base form have.
Money is uncountable, so use little; few and many go with plural nouns.
Reported questions use statement word order: how she had changed.

questions.before: If Mathilde had stayed at home, she
questions.rule: Third conditional result clause: would (not) have + past participle.
The past participle stunned describes how they felt; it pairs with by.

questions.before: The jeweller showed them two necklaces, but
questions.rule: For two things, use neither with a singular verb; every cannot take 'of', and all needs 'were'.
The determiner no comes right before the noun: no jewels.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the past continuous.
questions.rule: Past continuous: was/were + -ing form - were trembling.

questions.prompt: Make a guess about the past.
questions.rule: A sure guess about the past: must have + past participle.
In a reported question the verb comes after the subject: what the matter was.
would have + past participle in the result, had + past participle after if.

chat: Can I borrow your blue pen?
options: Sure, take it. It's on mine desk.
Sure, take it. It's on me desk.
Sure, take it. It's on my desk.
questions.rule: Before a noun, use the possessive determiner my, not mine or me.

chat: Did you give the invitation to Mrs Joshi?
options: Yes, I gave it to her.
Yes, I gived it to her.
Yes, I given it to her.
questions.rule: Give is irregular: past gave, past participle given.

chat: I can't find my phone anywhere!
options: You might have left it on the bus.
You might has left it on the bus.
You might have leave it on the bus.
questions.rule: A possible past event: might have + past participle - might have left.

options: She told that we had a test on Monday.
She told us that we had a test on Monday.
She said us that we had a test on Monday.
questions.rule: Told needs a person after it (told us); said does not take one directly.

chat: We missed the train by two minutes!
options: If we had left earlier, we would have caught it.
If we left earlier, we would have caught it.
If we had left earlier, we would caught it.
questions.rule: For an unreal past: If + had left, would have caught.

chat: Did the players get their jerseys?
options: Yes, each players got a jersey.
Yes, each player got an jersey.
Yes, each player got a jersey.
questions.rule: Each takes a singular noun, and jersey starts with a consonant sound, so a jersey.

chat: Anu didn't come to the party.
options: She can't have be ill. I saw her at the market.
She can't have been ill. I saw her at the market.
She can't had been ill. I saw her at the market.
questions.rule: To say something was impossible in the past: can't have + past participle - can't have been.

chat: Who told you about the change in the timetable?
options: Kunal told me that the timetable had been change.
Kunal told to me that the timetable had been changed.
Kunal told me that the timetable had been changed.
questions.rule: Told me (no 'to'), and the passive needs the past participle: had been changed.

questions.source: Loisel said to his wife, "Try and get a really beautiful dress."
options: Loisel told his wife to tried and get a really beautiful dress.
Loisel told his wife to try and get a really beautiful dress.
Loisel told to his wife try and get a really beautiful dress.
questions.rule: An order or advice is reported with told + person + to + base form.

questions.prompt: Change into the past continuous tense.
options: Mathilde were dancing at the party.
Mathilde was danced at the party.
Mathilde was dancing at the party.
questions.rule: Past continuous: was + -ing form with a singular subject - was dancing.

options: Mathilde did not had any jewels.
Mathilde did not have any jewels.
Mathilde did not have some jewel.
questions.rule: In negatives, some becomes any; after did not, use the base form have.

questions.source: I am sure that the guests enjoyed the party.
options: The guests must enjoyed the party.
The guests must have enjoyed the party.
The guests must had enjoyed the party.
questions.rule: Being sure about the past = must have + past participle.

questions.source: Loisel asked Mathilde, "Did you take his number?"
options: Loisel asked Mathilde if had she taken his number.
Loisel asked Mathilde if she has took his number.
Loisel asked Mathilde if she had taken his number.
questions.rule: Yes/no questions are reported with if/whether, statement order and backshift: she had taken.

questions.source: Loisel did not take the cab's number. He could not find the cab.
options: If Loisel took the cab's number, he could have found the cab.
If Loisel had taken the cab's number, he could have found the cab.
If Loisel had taken the cab's number, he could found the cab.
questions.rule: Imagining a different past: If + had + past participle, could have + past participle.

questions.source: If Mathilde had told her friend the truth, she would not have suffered so much.
options: Had Mathilde told her friend the truth, she would not suffered so much.
Had Mathilde tell her friend the truth, she would not have suffered so much.
Had Mathilde told her friend the truth, she would not have suffered so much.
questions.rule: Drop if and put had before the subject; the rest stays the same.

questions.prompt: Change into passive voice, beginning with 'Mathilde'.
questions.source: Madame Forestier lent Mathilde a diamond necklace.
options: Mathilde was lend a diamond necklace by Madame Forestier.
Mathilde is lent a diamond necklace by Madame Forestier.
Mathilde was lent a diamond necklace by Madame Forestier.
questions.rule: Simple past passive: was + past participle; the past participle of lend is lent.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: The story is in the past: came and drew (irregular past forms).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Countable plural nouns take many and few; much and little are for uncountable nouns. those ... were and one of them show the nouns are plural.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Modal + have (never 'of') + past participle: should have returned, can't have seen.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: would have + past participle (become); after had to, both verbs take the base form: rent ... and do.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Use who for a person, had borrowed (past participle), and both of her hands (plural).
